CFML Language Reference: Functions

CreateODBCDate

Converts a date/time value or date string into an ODBC date escape such as {d '1999-10-22'}. Any time part is dropped.

Category

Date and time functions

Syntax

CreateODBCDate(date)

Parameters

date
A date/time value or a string that can be converted to one.

Returns

A string in the form {d 'yyyy-mm-dd'}.

Usage

ODBC escapes are understood by every ODBC driver (and by the KoldFusion built-in engine), so they are the safest way to put a date into a CFQUERY without worrying about the database's own date syntax. Do not put quotes around the result in your SQL; the escape already contains them.

Example

Opens the example in a new window. The example runs on this server, so it only works when you browse from the server itself (127.0.0.1).
<CFSET Cutoff = CreateDate(1998, 1, 1)>
<CFOUTPUT>
<TABLE BORDER=1 CELLPADDING=3>
<TR><TH>Input</TH><TH>CreateODBCDate</TH></TR>
<TR><TD>CreateDate(1998, 1, 1)</TD><TD>#CreateODBCDate(Cutoff)#</TD></TR>
<TR><TD>"10/22/1999 9:42 PM"</TD><TD>#CreateODBCDate("10/22/1999 9:42 PM")#</TD></TR>
<TR><TD>Now()</TD><TD>#CreateODBCDate(Now())#</TD></TR>
</TABLE>
<P>In a query you would write:</P>
<PRE>
SELECT FirstName, LastName FROM Employees
WHERE StartDate &gt;= #CreateODBCDate(Cutoff)#
</PRE>
</CFOUTPUT>
